objective: Finish and independently verify the universal-agent-integration release candidate, fixing every reproduced release blocker without weakening Aperio Next governance or damaging user state.
expected_outcome: An evidence-backed release candidate that is genuinely usable for the explicitly verified host and platform scope, with exact limitations for everything unverified.
scope: Current feature branch implementation and diff against main
Python engine and native integration manager
Supported native host assets and project persistence
Disposable real-user workflow, fresh-session recovery, security review, documentation, commit, and push
exclusions: Publishing npm or PyPI packages or public releases
Deleting the legacy Aperio project, important user data, or foreign host configuration
Installing unrelated paid tools, bypassing permissions or governance, or claiming untested platforms and hosts
assumptions: The feature branch and existing untracked .aperio and audit-inputs content must be preserved
Live provider testing is bounded by installed binaries, authentication, quota, and host interfaces
macOS arm64 is the only locally executable operating-system scope unless another real environment is discovered
risks: Destructive or falsely successful partial lifecycle operations
Missing or duplicated durable project integration
Source-only tests masking broken installed artifacts
Approval, review, or evidence gate bypass
Unsupported host, platform, CI, or registry claims
strategy: Verify the baseline, reproduce every named P0 and security risk with focused adversarial fixtures, fix only confirmed gaps test-first, then exercise built artifacts and bounded live hosts through the daily-use journey before independently reviewing the final diff and recording scoped evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Inject failed engine installation/upgrade, failed skill/command regeneration, partial host-registration failure, and interrupted update; each must preserve or restore the last known-good engine and compatible integration assets, verify recovered identity and asset compatibility, and preserve previous project data and unrelated user configuration. Claim rollback only from actual injected-failure evidence.
Generated native integrations invoke the correct validated Aperio Next engine

A mandatory genuinely fresh Codex CLI session invokes native $aperio-next and proves discovery, activation, correct engine identity, actual aperio next execution, consented initialization, and a governed coding task in a disposable project. Another fresh session receives Continue the previous task and uses the engine to recover completed and pending work. Reading SKILL.md or launching a Python subprocess is insufficient. Codex is a primary mandatory acceptance target. Report Codex CLI and VS Code Codex extension results separately with exact blockers for unavailable environments; missing Codex evidence remains unmet.
Initialization, durable integration, governed execution, verification, and independent review work without bypasses

No known unresolved critical/high defect remains. A separate reviewer agent or independent fresh review session receives the complete final diff, acceptance criteria, and test evidence. The implementation author is not the sole reviewer. Require an explicit findings report with concrete security, reliability, and integration defects, file locations, reproduction steps, and assessment of governance/authorization boundaries, packaging, lifecycle, and persistent project instructions. Reproduce and fix all valid critical/high findings with regressions, repeat affected verification, and obtain independent follow-up review. If independence is unavailable, record the exact limitation and leave independent acceptance unmet; never self-certify independence. Independent review covers the complete final diff including final documentation; recheck subsequent changes before handoff. Report injected-failure rollback evidence, separate Codex CLI/VS Code results, and independent findings and resolutions. Missing mandatory evidence prevents a READY FOR DAILY USE verdict.
Final documentation, Git state, compatibility matrix, limitations, and quick-start are backed by newly executed evidence
verification_strategy: Run the full Python and Node suites; build and inspect clean wheel/npm artifacts; exercise isolated install, doctor, activation, update/repair, and uninstall; test new/existing projects and the governed coding workflow; launch bounded fresh native-agent sessions where available; run focused security regressions; and review the complete diff before commit and push.
